misconception_description: Student believes that loop variables are destroyed and are inaccessible after the loop completes.

solutions.generated_code:
program MatriksIdentitas
kamus
  n, i, j, terakhirI : integer
  baris : string
algoritma
  input(n)
  terakhirI <- 0
  for i <- 1 to n do
    terakhirI <- i
    baris <- ""
    for j <- 1 to n do
      if i == j then
        baris <- baris + "1 "
      else
        baris <- baris + "0 "
      endif
    endfor
    output(baris)
  endfor
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes loop variables (i, j, tup, etc.) are destroyed when their loops complete, so they create auxiliary variables (last_i, last_diag_i, last_diag_j) to "preserve" the values before the loops end. They update these preservation variables on each iteration, ensuring the values are saved. While unnecessary, this doesn't break the code's functionality - it just adds redundant variable assignments. The student genuinely believes this is the proper way to retain loop variable values, similar to how local variables in some languages/contexts might be scoped only to their block.
